main_text.p: discretas esse & disparatas. Et quamuis ratio, à Similitudine ducta, sit omnium maximè imbellis, quæ non robur, sed solùm lumen disputationi adferat; in hac tamen totus es, nec Rationem vllam vspiam vrges vehementiùs. Rectiùs Dialectici, qui Similitudinem ad genus docendi exotericum & populare accommodant, Cuius in acroamatico & accurato arguendi genere rarus ac ferè nullus est visus; sic enim Princeps Philosophorum, [illegible, ~20 letters] Haud igitur in tàm coacta Similitudine adeò acriter Tibi insistendum fuit, in qua (quod de Sabinis dicitur) quod voluisti somniasti.
main_text.head: II. ANIMADVERSIO.

head.i: Celebrem illam [CARNIS, & SPIRITVS] aduersus Principes detortum Similitudinem ab ipso Nazianzeno membratim refutari.

main_text.p: SImilitudinem hanc Carnis & Spiritus semel in libris de Pontifice obijcis; rursus repetis in Torto; in Responso ad Apologiam inculcas denuò; post contra Barclaium ingeris; atq; etiam insuper eam Lectori obtrudis in Epistola ad Anonymum: quam crambeh quinquies iam recoctam in hoc de Principum officio Tractatu reponis; ac si omnes fortunæ vestræ, & totius Causæ vestræ ædificiū hoc potissimum fundamento niteretur. Dabis (uti spero) mihi veniā, quùm sis in vrgenda hac Similitudine impendio prolixior atque impor tunior, si ego in ea refellenda maiorem operam insumam.

Greg. Nazianzenus spiritualem quidem Sacerdotū potestatem supra Principum anthoritatem, in merè spiritualibus, hòn minūs quàm spiritum carni (nec sanè imeritò) præferendam esse iudicauit. At Principes, quoad externam dignitatem, aut temporalem coercionem potestati Ecclesiasticæ neutiquam subiecit: tantum enim abest vt Gregorius, cognomento Theologus, tàm tetram [illegible, ~8 letters] Christianis propinaret, vt planè contrariam illi mentem fuisse, vel mores ipsius demonstrent.

page.notes: Doubtful or illegible: "crambeh" (printed form uncertain, possibly crambem); "impor tunior" printed with a gap at the line end, read as one word; the Greek after "Princeps Philosophorum" and the Greek word after "tetram" are too faint to read letter by letter; the Greek word after "tetram" may be a form of Iudaismum, not confirmed. Show-through text from the reverse side behind "quod voluisti somniasti" and the summary line was left out. The mark in the left margin beside "Greg. Nazianzenus" is an ornament, not text. The initial S of "Similitudinem" is a drop cap, joined as "SImilitudinem". Marginal note "Sect.VII." placed beside the summary line.
